ai.definition: Quadratic Voting Systems are a mechanism design technique that allows individuals to express the intensity of their preferences in voting by purchasing additional votes at an increasing cost.
ai.howItWorks: Voters have a budget with which they can purchase votes. The cost for each additional vote is the square of the number of votes already purchased, ensuring that the marginal cost increases as more votes are bought. This system aims to balance individual preferences with collective outcomes in a fairer manner than traditional voting methods.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing the issue of unequal influence in majority voting systems where those with more resources can disproportionately sway decisions.
ai.buildProcess: The implementation involves setting up a budget for each voter, determining the cost structure for additional votes, and establishing rules for casting and counting votes. This process is primarily software-based and requires no physical manufacturing steps.
ai.costDrivers: The primary cost drivers are the administration of the system, including setting budgets, managing transactions, and ensuring compliance with the quadratic pricing rule. These costs can vary widely depending on the scale and complexity of implementation.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is still in its early stages but shows potential for broader adoption as more case studies and real-world applications are developed.
ai.regulation: Currently, there is no specific regulation targeting Quadratic Voting Systems. However, they may fall under existing regulations related to elections or decision-making processes once implemented on a larger scale.
ai.risks: Potential risks include the complexity of implementation, ensuring equal access to voting budgets, and the potential for manipulation if not properly regulated.
ai.profitability: Profitability is currently uncertain as there are no established business models. However, it could potentially generate revenue through fees or licensing agreements with organizations implementing the system.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development may focus on refining the cost structure, improving user interfaces, and expanding to various applications beyond traditional voting systems.
ai.energyRequirements: Low energy requirements for operational power draw; manufacturing is minimal due to software-based implementation. However, ongoing operation requires server infrastructure which could be energy-intensive depending on scale.

subsystems.name: Eligibility and identity
subsystems.role: ensures each participant gets exactly one budget of voice credits — the hardest problem, since the mechanism is only fair if one person cannot vote many times.
parts: enrolment against a government ID, membership list or invite set
cryptographic credential (key pair) bound to that identity
uniqueness proof such as a nullifier so a credential can be used once without revealing who used it

subsystems.name: Credit wallet
subsystems.role: holds the fixed budget of voice credits and stops anyone spending more than they have.
parts: recovery path if a key is lost

subsystems.name: Ballot and cost engine
subsystems.role: implements the pricing rule — casting n votes on one option costs n² credits — and shows the voter the marginal cost of the next vote.
parts: integer arithmetic on credits to avoid rounding disputes

subsystems.name: Private submission
subsystems.role: lets people vote without their choices being linkable to their identity, which matters for coercible decisions.
parts: encryption of the ballot to the tallier
zero-knowledge proof that the ballot is well-formed and affordable

subsystems.name: Tallying and proof
subsystems.role: sums the votes, verifies every proof and publishes evidence that the arithmetic is correct.
parts: verifier that checks proofs without seeing individual ballots

subsystems.name: Matching pool (quadratic funding variant)
subsystems.role: applies the same square-root logic to subsidy rather than votes: a shared pool is split in proportion to the square of the sum of square roots of contributions, so many small supporters count for more than one large one.

buildSteps.title: Define the decision
buildSteps.detail: Fix the question, the options and who is eligible, because the pricing rule only makes sense against a closed set of choices.

buildSteps.title: Choose the budget and price scale
buildSteps.detail: Set the number of voice credits per voter and confirm the quadratic cost curve; this single parameter decides how strongly intensity of preference is rewarded versus breadth of support.

buildSteps.title: Issue credentials
buildSteps.detail: Give each eligible participant a key tied to a verified identity, plus one uniqueness marker, so that re-enrolment or a second account is detectable.

buildSteps.title: Build the client
buildSteps.detail: Ship a voting interface that shows credits spent and marginal cost live — voters routinely underestimate how fast the square grows.

buildSteps.title: Capture and encrypt ballots
buildSteps.detail: The client computes the proofs locally and sends only encrypted, eligibility-proven ballots to the server.

buildSteps.title: Verify and tally
buildSteps.detail: The tallier checks every proof, rejects over-budget ballots, and sums the votes; sums and proofs, not individual choices, are published.

buildSteps.title: Audit and publish
buildSteps.detail: Independent auditors re-run the tally from the published data; results and the audit trail go out together.

buildSteps.title: Review the parameter set
buildSteps.detail: After the vote, check whether turnout, concentration of credits and outcomes matched expectations, and adjust the budget for next time.

prerequisites.why: without one-person-one-budget, a wealthy or organised group can simply buy extra wallets and the quadratic pricing collapses.

pathway.milestone: small-scale deployments — community budgets, party and student ballots, online public-goods funding rounds
pathway.unlocks: real data on how voters behave when votes are priced.

pathway.milestone: integration with national or state digital-identity wallets
pathway.unlocks: eligibility at population scale without a central registrar watching every ballot.

pathway.milestone: advisory or budget-allocation votes in municipalities and large organisations
pathway.unlocks: evidence for whether intensity-weighted voting produces better decisions than one-person-one-vote.

pathway.milestone: hybrid systems where quadratic voting is used for some questions and conventional voting for others
pathway.unlocks: a realistic institutional role rather than a wholesale replacement for existing elections.
